name: Bachelor of Engineering (Civil) (Honours)
about: Four years in civil engineering with common first-year subjects that let you switch specialisation, up to 12 weeks of industry placement, an honours research project and an industry design project.

name: Bachelor of Science
about: Three years across the natural and physical sciences, from the sub-atomic to the planetary, building analytical methods, laboratory and field techniques and IT skills; taught across four campuses.

name: Bachelor of Politics, Philosophy and Economics
credential: Bachelor of Politics, Philosophy and Economics
about: A three-year degree combining political analysis, philosophical theory and economics, with a capstone course; run by the ANU College of Arts and Social Sciences.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
about: Four years that start with a shared Engineering Foundation Year, then a major such as Chemical, Civil and Construction, Electrical and Electronic, Mechanical, Mechatronic or Mining Engineering.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
about: A four-year honours engineering degree open to international students, with entry in Trimester 1 or Trimester 2 and full-time study.

name: Bachelor of Science
about: A three-year science degree covering a broad range of disciplines with practical skills, for international students starting in Trimester 1 or 2.

name: Bachelor of Science
about: A flexible first year lets you sample science, biomedicine, maths, engineering and IT subjects before you choose one of more than 40 majors; electives in business, languages and communication sit alongside.

name: Bachelor of Biomedicine
about: A health-science degree taught beside the Melbourne Biomedical Precinct, with 40+ hospitals and research institutes nearby; the usual route to graduate medicine, dentistry, physiotherapy or research.

name: Bachelor of Science
about: A flexible three-year science degree with majors in biological, biomedical, earth and environmental, mathematical and computational, and physical and chemical sciences, taught at Clayton.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
about: A four-year honours engineering degree with specialisations that include aerospace, biomedical, chemical and civil; the whole academic record is considered in selection.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
about: A four-year honours degree with ten specialisations from Civil and Mechanical to Machine Learning Systems and Medical, 60 days of work experience in an Australian engineering environment, and a double-degree option.

name: Bachelor of Business
about: A three-year business degree where you pick a major such as Finance, Marketing, Economics, Global Business, Entrepreneurship or Business Information Systems.

name: Bachelor of Computer Science
about: A three-year degree in designing software, applications and systems, building programming skills and specialising in different fields of computer science.

name: Bachelor of Advanced Computing
about: A four-year computing degree where you complete a major in Computer Science, Computational Data Science, Cybersecurity or Software Development, and can add a second major or a minor from a shared pool of 100+ majors.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
about: A business degree built on one major, such as Finance, Marketing, Accounting or Business Analytics, plus a second major or minor and open-learning units. Combines with Computing, Engineering, Law or Science.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
about: A four-year honours engineering degree across more than 20 engineering disciplines, with a flexible first year, project-based learning and industry training.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
about: UNSW Business School's core undergraduate degree, built around problem-solving and business for a sustainable society, with majors and double degrees to combine it with other fields.

name: Bachelor of Science
about: A three-year science degree with 16 extended majors, 26 majors and 35 minors; you can mix science and non-science courses in first year and combine it with 13 other programs.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
about: A four-year engineering degree with a flexible first year, then 6 core specialisations and 12 majors; programs can be combined with Science, Computer Science, Design, Arts and others.

name: Bachelor of Marine and Antarctic Science
credential: Bachelor of Marine and Antarctic Science
about: Three years in Hobart through the Institute for Marine and Antarctic Studies, building an understanding of marine environments across natural and social sciences, with units such as Ecology and Biology of Animals.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) (Flexible)
about: Four years of engineering in which the Flexible major lets you explore several disciplines in first year before choosing; accredited by Engineers Australia, with an industry practice stream.

name: Bachelor of Science
about: A three-year science degree with 29 majors, from agricultural science and anatomy to computer science, cybersecurity and data science, taught by UWA researchers.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
about: An industry-developed engineering degree at UWA built on three core principles, leading to the Honours qualification.

name: International Liberal Arts
about: A four-year liberal-arts degree taught entirely in English, in which you later choose between the Global Business, Global Studies and Global Connectivity programmes.

name: College of Asia Pacific Studies (APS)
about: Political systems, economies, societies and cultures of the Asia Pacific region, in three areas: culture, society and media; international relations; and global economy. A shared liberal-arts first year comes before major courses.

name: College of International Management (APM)
about: Business studied in four areas: strategic management and leadership, marketing, accounting and finance, and entrepreneurship and operations management. The college holds AACSB and AMBA accreditation.

name: College of Sustainability and Tourism (ST)
about: Sustainable societies through environmental resource management and sustainable tourism, with nine concentrations spanning development, tourism, environment and entrepreneurship, and learning beyond the classroom.

name: Human Sciences International Undergraduate Degree Program
about: An English-medium degree from the School of Human Sciences with a small intake. After foundation courses you focus on Diversity and Inclusion Studies, Japan Studies, or Political and Global Studies, ending in a fourth-year thesis.

name: Integrated Science Program (ISP)
about: A science programme for international students: everyone studies maths, physics, chemistry and biology at university level for six months, then joins Physics, Chemistry or Biological Sciences in the School of Science. A 3.5-year fast track is possible.

name: Modern Japanese Studies Program (MJSP)
about: A four-year bachelor's on contemporary Japanese society and culture, taught in English. You start in October 2027 with a six-month beginners' Japanese course; the bachelor's itself starts in April 2028.

name: Liberal Arts
about: One bachelor's in liberal arts with 31 majors across humanities, social sciences and natural sciences; you declare a major before third year. You enter through English but must also complete the Japanese Language Program to graduate.

name: PEARL (Economics)
about: The Faculty of Economics' September-entry programme (Program in Economics for Alliances, Research and Leadership): economics studied wholly in English and finished in four years, for a BA in Economics.

name: GIGA Program
about: An English-based BA at the Shonan Fujisawa campus across Policy Management or Environment and Information Studies, mixing technology, design, business and policy. You can finish wholly in English; Japanese courses with English support are optional.

name: International Undergraduate Program (iUP)
credential: Bachelor's degree in your chosen major
about: A six-month preparatory course in intensive Japanese, then a four-year bachelor's in one of nine faculties, such as Science, Engineering or Economics. The first two years can be in English or Japanese; the last two are mainly in Japanese.

name: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
about: Electricity, electronics, communication, data science and computers in one programme, from power systems and sensing to AI, networks and security; taught wholly in English apart from Japanese classes.

name: Applied Chemistry
about: Materials with structure and function controlled at atomic and molecular level, covering organic, inorganic and biomolecular chemistry for IT, environmental, nano and biotechnology; taught in English.

name: Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
about: Mechanical engineering across precision instruments, robots, automobiles, rockets and energy technology, in the monozukuri tradition of making things; taught in English apart from Japanese classes.

name: Civil Engineering
about: Social infrastructure such as water and sewage, roads and ports, plus restoring damaged natural environments, with hardware and software for building design, urban planning and soil and water environment; taught in English.

name: Bioresource and Bioenvironment
about: School of Agriculture's International Undergraduate Program, taught entirely in English: basic and applied sciences, natural and social, behind bio-production, bio-function and bio-environment. Apply under Type B if you studied outside Japan.

name: Interdisciplinary Science and Innovation
about: A school without humanities-science boundaries, stressing communication, design thinking, data analysis and project management. The programme is bilingual: classes run in English and Japanese, not English alone.

name: Automotive Engineering
about: Mechanical engineering with an automotive focus, drawing on Nagoya's industry ties: electromechanical systems, micro- and nano-scale technology, aerospace and energy, with early courses on maths and physics.

name: Automotive Engineering
about: Electrical, electronic and information engineering for the automotive field, built on basic engineering and core electrical subjects, then advanced automotive technology.

name: Physics
about: Four years of physics taught entirely in English by the School of Science, from particle physics and condensed matter to astrophysics and plasma physics, in small classes of typically 5 to 15.

name: Chemistry
about: Chemistry in the School of Science: foundational, organic and inorganic chemistry in the first three years, with research across engineering, agriculture, pharmacy and medicine.

name: Chemistry
about: Chemistry in the School of Engineering: an interdisciplinary programme bridging materials science and the natural sciences, with chemistry, biology, physics and mathematics.

name: Biological Science
about: A joint programme of the School of Science and School of Agricultural Sciences preparing future researchers across fundamental and applied biology, including molecular, cellular and developmental biology.

name: Biological Science
about: Applied bioscience in the School of Agricultural Sciences: applied microbiology, biotechnology, food and nutrition, applied biochemistry and plant sciences.

name: Social Science
about: Law and political science taught wholly in English, within a joint School of Law and School of Economics programme on political science, law, economics, business and information science.

name: Social Science
about: Economics with a grounding in macro- and microeconomics, then management theory, accounting, public policy and urban economics, within the joint Social Science programme taught in English.

name: Japan-in-Asia Cultural Studies
about: The culture and history of Japan and its relations with other East Asian countries, stressing cultural history, cinema and visual culture, and literature, taught in English in the School of Humanities.

name: Liberal Arts
about: The Faculty of Liberal Arts (FLA) teaches in English and awards a BA in Liberal Arts, with first-year entry in spring and autumn.

name: Sophia Program for Sustainable Futures (SPSF)
about: English-taught BAs in seven fields: Journalism, Education, Sociology, Economics, Management, International Relations and Area Studies. You name your field when applying; Global Studies has no third-year transfer.

name: Digital Green Technology
about: A Bachelor of Engineering in Digital Green Technology in the Faculty of Science and Technology, taught in English, replacing the Green Science and Green Engineering programmes. About half of admitted students are expected to be international.

name: Gateway College
about: An English-taught undergraduate college with a Humanities and Social Sciences track and a STEM track. You study interdisciplinary courses first and declare a major from the third year; with a few exceptions all classes are in English.

name: International Social Studies
about: A degree earned wholly through English-taught classes, analysing political, economic and cultural issues in international society. You apply to the College of Social Sciences or International Studies; the other is your automatic second choice.

name: Biological Sciences
about: A College of Biological Sciences degree in the English-only Interdisciplinary Program of Life and Environmental Sciences, giving a firm base and specialised knowledge in the life sciences.

name: Agro-Biological Resource Sciences
about: A College of Agro-Biological Resource Sciences degree in the English-only Interdisciplinary Program of Life and Environmental Sciences, on the sustainable use of agro-biological resources and the environment.

name: Geoscience
about: A College of Geoscience degree in the English-only Interdisciplinary Program of Life and Environmental Sciences, covering earth and environmental sciences.

name: Interdisciplinary Engineering
about: Science and engineering taught in English from interdisciplinary angles, aimed at the next-generation smart society. Admission looks for basic maths, English and aptitude for engineering.

name: Global Issues
about: An international programme taught in English on global issues: earth environment, social diversity and inclusiveness, risk and security, and human health and wellbeing, drawing on the humanities and sciences.

name: UTokyo College of Design
about: A single five-year programme combining a bachelor's and a master's, with all classes in English. Students build their own pathways across disciplines using design approaches, and take long internships in Japan or overseas.

name: Political Science and Economics
about: Three English-taught degrees in one school: Political Science, Economics, and Global Political Economy, which splits coursework evenly between the two. Small discussion seminars of 5 to 15 students run throughout.

name: Transnational and Interdisciplinary Studies in Social Innovation (TAISI)
about: An English-based programme in the School of Social Sciences that trains students as social innovators and agents of change, approaching global issues across disciplines. It awards a BA in Social Sciences.

name: International Liberal Studies
about: A broad liberal-arts degree taught in English, set up in 2004, for students who want to range across fields. You choose Study Plan 1 or 2 by language background; Plan 1 includes a compulsory year abroad.

name: Global Studies in Japanese Cultures Program (JCulP)
about: English-taught study of Japanese culture in all its diversity, with a focus on Japanese literature, alongside Japanese students in Tokyo. It awards a BA in Literature.

name: Fundamental Science and Engineering
about: Two English-taught majors: Mathematical Sciences, from the fundamentals of science to specialist mathematical theory, and Computer Science and Communications Engineering. Flexible minors are possible.

name: Creative Science and Engineering
about: Two English-taught engineering majors, Mechanical Engineering and Civil and Environmental Engineering, with a curriculum from general engineering courses to specialised theory and practice.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
about: A four-year, 480-point honours degree. You study a broad engineering base in Part I, then specialise in one of ten fields, from civil, mechanical and software to biomedical and mechatronics engineering.

name: Bachelor of Science, Psychology major
about: A 360-point Bachelor of Science with a Psychology major: quantitative and qualitative approaches with laboratory or field work, and a capstone course communicating psychology through grant proposals, podcasts and print.

name: Bachelor of Education (Teaching)
about: A full-time, 360-point degree to become a certificated teacher in New Zealand, specialising in early childhood, primary or Maori-medium teaching, with 80 days of teaching experience in year three.

name: Bachelor of International Hospitality Management
about: A three-year, 360-point degree on how hospitality businesses run: food and beverage, accommodation, human resources, strategy and marketing, ending with workplace experience on a project with an organisation.

name: Bachelor of Sport, Exercise and Health
credential: Bachelor of Sport, Exercise and Health
about: A flexible 360-point degree on sport, movement, leadership, physical education, health and exercise science, with workplace experience at an industry partner and room to combine sport with other subjects such as journalism.

name: Bachelor of Engineering with Honours (international pathway)
about: An accelerated route for high-achieving international students: pre-university study from July, a term and a summer of foundation courses on campus, then three full years in your chosen engineering discipline.

name: Bachelor of Forestry Science
about: A professional 480-point degree combining core science with management, commerce and technology, with field stations near Arthur's Pass and Westport and 90 days of practical forestry work experience.

name: Bachelor of Viticulture and Oenology
about: A three-year degree in the science behind grape and wine production, from vineyard soils and plant science to wine quality assessment, with work in Lincoln's own vineyards and 18 weeks of industry placements.

name: Bachelor of Agricultural Science
about: A four-year science degree on farming systems, animal and plant production, soil and nutrient management and sustainability, with an Honours route in the fourth year that adds a research project.

name: Bachelor of Landscape Architecture
about: A four-year degree in landscape design, ecology and planning for urban and rural settings, taught in on-campus studios with real projects, accredited by the New Zealand Institute of Landscape Architects.

name: Bachelor of Veterinary Science (pre-selection semester)
about: Five years in total on the Manawatu campus. A six-month open-entry pre-selection semester from February decides, with selection assessments, who enters the 4.5-year professional phase that starts in July.

name: Bachelor of Aviation
about: A three-year degree for professional pilots that builds a Commercial Pilot Licence with multi-engine and instrument rating into university study at an internationally recognised training facility.

name: Bachelor of Veterinary Nursing
about: A three-year degree combining veterinary nursing knowledge and clinical skills with extensive workplace experience; years 1 and 2 are on campus and year 3 is online with a work placement.

name: Bachelor of Architectural Studies (Architectural Technology) or (Interior Architecture)
about: Builds skills in drawing, computer-aided design, building science, construction and communication, leading to work as an architectural technologist or interior architect, or to further study to become a registered architect.

name: Bachelor of Construction (Quantity Surveying)
about: Trains construction professionals to price and manage construction projects, with the technical, work-ready skills for roles in quantity surveying.

name: Bachelor of Applied Management
about: A business degree built around industry experience, with an internship semester in the third year in which you complete a research project inside a real business.

name: Bachelor of Applied Management (Accounting)
about: An applied accounting qualification with case studies, applied assignments and a workplace-based industry project, aimed at becoming a chartered accountant or a CPA Australia certified accountant.

name: Bachelor of Visual Arts
about: A first year of core art courses, methodology and art history, then one of seven studio disciplines, including ceramics and jewellery, in which to develop your own practice.

name: Bachelor of Design (Fashion)
about: A fashion degree built on sustainability, industry connections and hands-on courses, where you develop your own style and identity as a designer.

name: Bachelor of Design (Communication)
about: Teaches you to craft ideas and tell stories through still and moving images, text, sound and interactive media, with community and client projects focused on social and environmental change.

name: Bachelor of Design (Product)
about: Teaches you to design products, services and systems with human needs and sustainability at the core, building and testing prototypes to develop conceptualisation and drawing skills.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
about: A broad first year in IT, then a focus in software development, IT infrastructure, network engineering or alternative digital platforms, with the option of a game development focus and industry projects.

name: Bachelor of Engineering Technology
about: An Engineering New Zealand accredited degree in civil, mechanical or electrical engineering, building skills in management, economics, communication and problem-solving.

name: Bachelor of Culinary Arts
about: Combines technical cooking skills, creative design tools and food business practice, learned by hands-on experience in the kitchen.

name: Bachelor of Social Services (Specialty)
about: Prepares you to work as a social services professional in New Zealand, with self-awareness, an understanding of Te Tiriti o Waitangi and the communication skills to support diverse people.

name: Bachelor of Midwifery
about: A four-year degree leading to registration as a midwife in New Zealand, with theory, real-life midwifery experience, online learning and compulsory block courses in Dunedin or Waikanae.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
about: A degree in nursing practice, human behaviour, pharmacology and body systems, with a simulation suite and practice placements, leading to the State Final Examination.

name: Bachelor of Occupational Therapy
about: Centred on working with people, with five placements for practice experience, leading to registration as an occupational therapist in New Zealand.

name: Bachelor of Applied Science
about: A degree built on practical experience and problem-based learning in sport, exercise and health, plus communication, academic writing and project management, with community projects.

name: Health Sciences First Year (HSFY)
credential: First year towards a health degree
about: The required first step to Dentistry, Medicine, Pharmacy, Physiotherapy and Medical Laboratory Science. Seven papers on the body and health, then a competitive second-year selection based on your HSFY results.

name: Exercise and Sport Science
about: A Bachelor of Science major on biomechanics, motor control and learning, physiology and psychology, aligned with accrediting bodies in New Zealand and Australia, with a practicum of clinical, lab or field experience.

name: Bachelor of Accounting
about: A three-year degree in accounting and finance principles, tax and business law, using software such as Xero and Power BI, with a final-year work placement. It meets the academic requirements for CA ANZ and CPA pathways.

name: Bachelor of Applied Science (Animal Behaviour and Welfare, and Biodiversity Management)
about: A double major that joins animal behaviour and welfare with biodiversity management, with courses on animal health and husbandry, behaviour modification, conservation and how ecosystems work.

name: Bachelor of Applied Science (Animal Behaviour and Welfare)
about: Covers animal health and husbandry, conservation, behaviour modification and human-animal interactions, preparing you for a career in the animal care sector.

name: Bachelor of Applied Science (Biodiversity Management)
about: Explores how ecosystems support biological diversity and how managers respond to human impact, including the social, cultural and policy frameworks behind management decisions.

name: Bachelor of Architectural Studies
about: The first step towards an architecture career: drawing, design and graphic presentation, site analysis, environmental sustainability, building law and construction technology, with a Maori perspective on design.

name: Bachelor of Business (Management)
about: Builds management, leadership and problem-solving skills through hands-on projects: leading people, driving projects and contributing to an organisation's success.

name: Bachelor of Business (Marketing)
about: Teaches consumer behaviour and marketing planning, with industry-based learning projects for organisations that match your specialisation.

name: Bachelor of Computing Systems
about: A three-year degree that builds professional adaptive skills for the computing industry, including developing and deploying software applications for mobile devices.

name: Bachelor of Construction (Construction Economics)
about: Trains quantity surveyors: estimating, evaluating subcontractor tenders, managing construction costs and cash flow, and agreeing final project accounts.

name: Bachelor of Construction (Construction Management)
about: Prepares you to organise and manage activities on a construction site, from management structures and supply chains to contract law and tendering.

name: Bachelor of Construction (Property Development)
about: Follows property development from concept to sale, covering valuation, financing, portfolio management, procurement, tendering, and property and contract law.

name: Bachelor of Design and Contemporary Art
credential: Bachelor of Design and Contemporary Art
about: A hands-on degree whose first year of discovery and experimentation leads to a specialist path in art and design, building technical skills through making.

name: Bachelor of Engineering Technology (Civil)
about: A three-year degree in civil engineering practice with pathways in environmental, geotechnical, water, roading and transportation, or structural engineering, plus computer modelling and project management.

name: Bachelor of Engineering Technology (Electrical)
about: A three-year degree in electrical and electronic engineering with a specialisation in electronics, power or mechatronics, covering engineering computing, mechanics, mathematics and design.

name: Bachelor of Landscape Architecture
about: A four-year degree that joins science, technology, art and design to shape urban and rural environments, from urban design and transport infrastructure to waterfronts and coastal projects.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
about: A three-year degree to become a registered nurse, balancing theory and practice, with human biology, nursing skills and research-informed practice taught at the Waitakere campus.

name: Bachelor of Performing and Screen Arts (Acting for Screen and Theatre)
credential: Bachelor of Performing and Screen Arts
about: Three years of training in voice, body and character, with accents, audition technique and the professional skills to work as an artist in screen and theatre.

name: Bachelor of Performing and Screen Arts (Contemporary Dance)
credential: Bachelor of Performing and Screen Arts
about: A full-time dance degree covering contemporary dance, street dance, ballet, choreography, improvisation and professional practice such as self-employment and grant writing.

name: Bachelor of Performing and Screen Arts (Screen Arts)
credential: Bachelor of Performing and Screen Arts
about: Three years behind the camera: specialise in cinematography, editing, production, screenwriting or directing, with collaborative projects alongside the Acting and Dance students.

name: Bachelor of Social Practice
about: A four-year degree preparing you for employment and registration in social work and community development, with basic counselling skills.

name: Bachelor of Teaching (Early Childhood Education)
about: A field-based degree for becoming an early childhood teacher: you work at least 12 hours a week in an early childhood centre and spend two days a week on campus.

name: Bachelor of Veterinary Nursing
about: Builds on the Diploma in Veterinary Nursing: animal nursing fundamentals in year one, then voluntary registration and the clinical skills to work in a veterinary team.
